[Music] The Lord who raised the dead is the one who saved my son from death.
I stand here today as a witness before the Lord and before our Blessed Mother during this apparition.
My name is Sheeba Francis. I’m here today for the sake of my son, Danish.
I come from the Rosary Queen Church in Thiruthipuram, which is in Ernakulam district.
On December 26, 2019, I made a covenant. When I heard about the many blessings Mother Mary gave
I said I belong to Mother Mary’s church and I serve the Mother, so I was told not to go to the Kreupasanam.
But my heart would not allow it, and I entered the Kreupasanam. It was during my son’s plus two studies.
I came here to understand how his further studies would progress, and I made a covenant and prayed.
After returning home, I started reading the Bible for half an hour daily and visiting the church every day.
I only used to go to the church on Saturdays and Sundays, but from then on I began going daily.to my siblings through the covenant, I too made the decision.
Through divine strength, I have gained a lot of power sometimes. Whatever divine power I prayed with,
both the Mother and Jesus would grant it to me. Since then, I have gone through many pains and illnesses.
At that time, my brothers would say to me, you do a lot of work for the church,
and you should have gotten rid of your illnesses by now. But I would say, whenever I get sick,
being able to endure it more strengthens me more. After Corona, I didn’t come to renew myself. So
time passed, and in June, when my son had exams, I joined him, while he was taking his exams.
When he went to school for an extra week of exams, he came back saying he had stomach pain.
He went to the bathroom and told me, “Mom, I’m not going to class today,
I have a stomach ache.” I told him, “Son, you should go to class, the next week there’s an exam.” He went to bed.
Around 12 o’clock, he got up and went to wash the vehicle, he never washes the vehicle—the older brother usually does that.
That day at 12 o’clock, for some reason, he switched the chain on and started washing the bike by hand.
While washing it with a cloth, his hand got cut and about half of the skin was torn off. At that time, nobody was home; his elder brother was out.
His brother had gone out, so he went to the road to check if anyone was around.
When he found no one, he came back and called his friends on the phone. They came to take him to the hospital.
By the time they arrived, his elder brother had come and taken him to the hospital. I was at work and was informed.
When I reached the hospital, I told him, “Son, Mother saved you from a great danger. If you had fallen from the bike, a serious accident could have happened to you.”
“Mother even stopped a finger of yours from being lost. Son, I was very happy and thanked God.”
At the hospital, they said he needed surgery and scheduled it for the next day.
That night, he told his brother, “My piece is there; the doctor is checking it,” he said.
A large piece was lying near the bike. When it was taken to the doctor, he said it was too late.
After that, happily, I sent him into the operation theater because I fully believed my Mother had saved my son from a great danger.
The surgery involved taking tissue from under the ring finger, sewing it, and attaching it back inside.
After 15 days, they took it out, shaped it, stitched it, and sent him home.
When it healed, they told him to keep loosening it. After loosening it, the next day when I checked, there was a large swelling on his hand at the operated site.
Then I called the doctor again and asked. The doctor said to come and see him.
The doctor gave antibiotics and said it was an infection. After eight days of antibiotics...
After eight days, another swelling appeared nearby. When the swelling appeared, we brought him back again.
For about a month, he kept taking antibiotics. Then the doctor said if there was grease or something inside, it could mix with the blood.
That’s why they gave medicine to purify the blood. Still, it did not reduce.
Then the doctor said we need to do an open surgery again.
They opened the stitched operated area, cleaned it again, and closed it for the second time.
The doctor said the next day he would go to Rajagiri Hospital. I had seen that the doctor was at Chalakka Medical College Hospital but was moving to Rajagiri.
So before going, he said they could do the operation that day itself, and after the operation, he left for Rajagiri.
Then he called me and said they had inserted a tube to drain the pus and blood from the hand, and the doctor said they would remove it the next day.
When we went to remove it the next day, the doctor said it was still there and advised to remove it when the time was right.
Even after days passed, it was not removed.
The doctor said he removed all stitches and that there was no more problem. When he came home and checked, he said there was still a tube inside.
I told him, “Son, that must be skin or something.” He said, “No.”
Mom said it was moving. I told my sister’s daughter, who is a nurse in the operation theater at Chalakka Hospital.
Because she is experienced as a doctor’s nurse. When I informed the doctor, he said to come to the hospital the next day to remove it.
Then she said, “I will remove it myself.” She took it and went to the hospital the next day.
When she removed the tube, a large opening was visible. I cried immediately and prayed to Mother,
saying, “Mother, I will come to Kreupasanam. Mother, I will renew my covenant.”
I came here, renewed my covenant, and brought holy oil with me. One night while praying, I applied the holy oil on my son’s hand.
I rubbed it and removed the faith bandage. When I checked the next day, the wound had completely dried.
I could see no scars or marks. It was fully healed. I gave this testimony.
The next month when I came here, I said I would bring my son, but he did not come.
He said his friends would tease him if he came to testify, so he stayed away. Since then, I started praying again.
When it was time to renew the covenant a second and third time, I said, “Mother, when I go there, everyone will ask why I didn’t testify. I have no testimony about Jesus.”
So I did not renew it for two or three months. Due to various reasons and because of building my house, I moved away.
Then on June 16th, his hand got injured again. On the 14th, I asked him, “Son, hasn’t it been a year since your hand was cut?” He said, “Yes, Mom.”
On Saturday, he went to work. On Sunday night, around 11 o’clock,
he was working at a company that ships prawns. He worked in the freezer section, handling the current line.
While pulling the current line, he suddenly got an electric shock and fell into the water.
Another son held him. He was conscious but lying on the side he fell on, with foam and froth coming from his mouth.
The manager came downstairs hearing the noise. This manager never came on Sundays, but God brought him there at that time.
Hearing the cry, the manager thought it was an electric shock and rushed upstairs.
When he saw him unconscious, he called the fire service. They came and gave CPR.
When he arrived at the hospital, they said he had very little life left.
We were informed. When we reached the hospital, seeing him was heartbreaking for me.
His eyes were open, mouth half-open, lying like he was dead. I asked a doctor, “Is my son dead?” I was about to pray.
I held Mother's medal and anointing oil in my hand, hoping and praying.
I placed the medal on his neck. I applied oil three times and recited the faith declaration.
It was the faith declaration of my broken heart. My life partner also prayed. The doctor said—
took Ammachi and sat her down. I took her to the veranda of Medical Trust Hospital.
Sitting in the veranda of Medical Trust Hospital, I held her hand and recited the Creed (profession of faith) and prayed.
That moment I realized how powerful the Creed is; every time I recited it, my Mother was strengthening me.
A Muslim girl who saw this told me, "Sister, there is a chapel upstairs, come there to pray."
She took me to that chapel, and there, my life partner and I knelt and kept reciting the Creed.
Everyone passing by looked at us and said, "May their prayers be answered, Lord."
Later, those who saw me said that to me.
In our village, when people heard that my son had died, they started coming to our door, saying he was dead.
My siblings came to comfort me, and I told them, "My son is alive and is in the hospital."
I told them, "My son will never die now; I have full faith that life will be given to him."
When they heard this, they were amazed. Still, I continued praying.
The next day, early morning, it was said that he could breathe without the help of the ventilator.
All the doctors said to my elder son that his life was only 1%, 99% he had already died.
If he is living with that 1%, he is in a coma; he is lying weak and inactive.
They asked him if he was willing to donate organs, and he ran out crying.
They called him again to see him one last time, but he did not stay; he ran away, and the doctors gave up.
At that moment, my Gracious Mother and Jesus were beside my son comforting him.
Soon he started breathing steadily and taking some breaths on his own.
The nurses came and said, "He has started breathing."
At that moment, I told my brother, "Let’s go to Kreupasanam now, son, we can go to Kreupasanam now."
We got into the car immediately and came to Kreupasanam
When I went outside, a woman came to my kitchen with a garland; I took it and thanked the Mother.
I placed the garland around the Mother’s neck. I brought my son’s photo along with me.
I told the audience here, "My son is exactly like this, and I wanted to see my father once more, but he had gone away."
So I placed the photo here in the chapel and knelt down and prayed; my brother and I recited the Creed 33 times.
I did not know the Creed was so powerful until then.
I kept reciting the Creed and said, "Let’s go," and got into the car.
After traveling a bit, my elder son called and said, "Mother, Danikutty’s eyes opened; Ammachi, please check."
I cannot thank my Lord enough. I was so happy I was jumping and praising Jesus.
I went to Jesus and then to the chapel and thanked Him. I kept thanking Him throughout the following days.
On the third day, he was taken out of ICU, and I was told to pay a bill and leave.
When I entered ICU, the nurses told me they didn’t expect to get him out in this condition.
So, on the third day, they shifted him from ICU to the room. Then the doctor told me, "Do not make him walk; he must stay in bed all the time."
They said, "If he needs to go to the bathroom or urinate, just put a pot; no need to get him up."
I helped him with all these. After an hour, he said he wanted to go to the bathroom.
I told him not to go, because the doctor said so.
I went and got a pot from the nurse and helped him urinate.
But he refused the pot and insisted on going to the bathroom himself.
I and my sister’s daughter held him firmly by both hands and took him to the bathroom.
As soon as he entered, he slammed the door, and we got scared.
Then he walked out alone. The children were shocked to see him walk into the bathroom all by himself.
The next day the doctor came and said, "Slowly try to make him walk." He jumped up and walked running.
What my son achieved was a great miracle; it was done by the Mother.
I used to attend the Divine Liturgy daily.
The power of that Divine Liturgy is so great, I prayed daily with my father for 38 years.
Because of the merit of that offering and the Divine Liturgy, I prayed and cried, "Please heal my son."
I realized that the Divine Liturgy we offer every day before God is great in healing my son.
I understood that every rosary we offer is powerful in the presence of God; otherwise, my son
would not have returned today—I am fully certain of that. Every day, I thank and keep thanking Mother, praying daily.
